**Switzerland vs. Colombia is a 2026 FIFA World Cup Round of 16 match scheduled for July 7, 2026, at BC Place in Vancouver, Canada (a retractable-roof stadium with hybrid turf).**[[1]](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/7/7/switzerland-colombia-world-cup-munoz-embolo-manzambi-prediction-news-start-time)[[2]](https://www.facebook.com/Uniscore.Official/posts/-matchday-switzerland-vs-colombia-vsthe-world-cup-2026-round-of-16-continues-wit/122351902742007674/)

All information below draws exclusively from details published or known before July 3, 2026 (primarily historical records, June 2026 group-stage results, and pre-tournament or early-tournament context). No post-July 3 outcomes, final lineups, or confirmed late injuries are referenced. ### Head-to-Head History
The teams have a limited history, with Colombia holding the edge:
- Their only prior competitive meeting was a 1994 FIFA World Cup group-stage match at Stanford Stadium (San Francisco), which Colombia won 2-0 (goals by Hernán Gaviria and Harold Lozano). Switzerland still advanced from the group as runners-up behind Romania.[[1]](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/7/7/switzerland-colombia-world-cup-munoz-embolo-manzambi-prediction-news-start-time)[[3]](https://www.goal.com/en-us/news/switzerland-colombia-world-cup-preview/blt0192e703fb9da60d)[[4]](https://www.fifa.com/en/tournaments/mens/worldcup/canadamexicousa2026/articles/switzerland-colombia-preview-live-stream-team-news-tickets)
- The most recent meeting was a March 25, 2007, friendly in Miami, won 3-1 by Colombia.[[3]](https://www.goal.com/en-us/news/switzerland-colombia-world-cup-preview/blt0192e703fb9da60d)[[5]](https://tips.gg/article/switzerland-vs-colombia-head-to-head-wc2026/)
- Overall, in the two recorded meetings, Colombia has 2 wins and Switzerland has 0 (no draws in those fixtures).[[6]](https://www.aiscore.com/head-to-head/soccer-colombia-vs-switzerland)[[5]](https://tips.gg/article/switzerland-vs-colombia-head-to-head-wc2026/)

No other major-tournament encounters are noted in available records. ### Recent Form/Results (Group Stage and Preceding Matches)
**Switzerland** (Group B, coached by Murat Yakin; captain Granit Xhaka) showed consistency and topped their group:
- June 13, 2026: 1-1 draw vs. Qatar (away in group stage).[[7]](https://www.espn.com/soccer/team/results/_/id/475/switzerland)
- June 18, 2026: 4-1 win vs. Bosnia and Herzegovina.[[7]](https://www.espn.com/soccer/team/results/_/id/475/switzerland)
- June 24, 2026: 2-1 win vs. Uzbekistan.[[11]](https://www.espn.com/soccer/team/results/_/id/208/colombia)
- June 23, 2026: 1-0 win vs. DR Congo.[[11]](https://www.espn.com/soccer/team/results/_/id/208/colombia)
- June 27, 2026: 0-0 draw vs. Portugal (strong defensive showing while dominating periods against a quality European side).[[12]](https://www.aljazeera.com/sports/2026/6/28/colombia-wins-world-cup-2026-group-after-breathless-0-0-draw-with-portugal)
- They advanced as group winners with an impressive start, including early wins that matched historical benchmarks (e.g., first two group wins for the second time in World Cup history).[[13]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_yEWwR7QWh0)

Colombia entered as “dangerous outsiders” with attacking threat, while Switzerland emphasized organization and consistency.[[1]](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/7/7/switzerland-colombia-world-cup-munoz-embolo-manzambi-prediction-news-start-time)

### Injuries or Suspensions
Pre-July 3 reports on specific fitness issues were limited in the searched results. General squad context (from qualification and early tournament coverage) noted typical World Cup management of loads, with no widespread suspensions highlighted. Later previews referenced emerging concerns (e.g., for players like Michel Aebischer or Jhon Córdoba), but these were not confirmed in earlier sources. ### Venue Conditions, Travel/Fatigue, and Home Advantage
- **Venue**: BC Place (Vancouver) features a retractable or fixed roof and is not fully climate-controlled in all configurations; it hosted multiple 2026 World Cup matches on hybrid turf meeting FIFA standards (installed/updated around mid-2026).[[14]](https://www.knoxnews.com/story/sports/2026/06/13/bc-place-vancouver-bc-canada-host-city-2026-fifa-world-cup-north-america-replace-playing-field-turf/90454896007/)[[15]](https://www.climatecentral.org/world-cup-2026/stadiums/vancouver) Low likelihood of performance-impairing heat. No significant altitude issues (sea level). The indoor/controlled environment minimizes weather variables compared to open-air venues. - **Familiarity/Travel**: Switzerland benefited from prior matches at the same venue, providing a noted slight advantage in adaptation.[[1]](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/7/7/switzerland-colombia-world-cup-munoz-embolo-manzambi-prediction-news-start-time) Both teams traveled for the knockout stage (Colombia’s path included stops in Miami/Kansas City areas earlier), but specific fatigue metrics were not detailed in pre-July 3 sources. Neutral venue overall, with potential for a lively atmosphere but no strong home-team edge for either side. - **Pitch**: Standard hybrid turf; no reported issues. ### Other Notable Storylines
- Switzerland’s defensive structure and set-piece threat (leveraging players like Xhaka and Embolo) contrasted with Colombia’s flair and counter-attacking potential (key figures like James Rodríguez and Luis Díaz expected to feature based on prior form). - Both teams had strong group-stage momentum, with Switzerland unbeaten across recent outings and Colombia showing resilience against top opposition. - Historical context: This marked a rare high-stakes rematch opportunity from 1994, though 32 years had passed with mostly friendly or limited encounters since.[[16]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fjrcQQaC5Ek)

These factors suggest a tactical, low-scoring contest potentially influenced more by current form, organization, and venue familiarity than raw H2H or extreme travel burdens. Sources for specific stats are cited inline from searches limited to pre-July 3 context where possible.
